equity_bridge.item: Pension and postretirement liability, after tax at 23%
equity_bridge.note: 405.7 at 30 Sep 2026, mostly unfunded OPEB (FY2025 10-K: OPEB net underfunded 435.1, pension 34.1 excluding overfunded plans)

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: net sales 3yr CAGR of 1.35% offset by the guided FY2026 decline and five years of falling volume
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-6.9% 3yr, -3.8% 5yr) diverges from revenue by far more than 30% and is not usable as a growth anchor: it reflects the US$3,645.7m Americas goodwill impairment in Q3-2025 plus buybacks, not operating shrinkage.
historical_growth.notes: 3yr = FY2022 to FY2025, 5yr = FY2020 to FY2025. Revenue 3yr is on net sales (10,701.0 -> 11,140.8); revenue 5yr is on gross sales (11,723.8 -> 13,040.3) because FY2020 net sales is not in the kpis table. EPS CAGRs are null: GAAP EPS was negative in FY2022 (-0.81) and FY2025 (-10.75) on impairments. FCF CAGRs are on the owner-FCF series (reported FCF less SBC; no interest strip, net debt): FY2020 1,096.7, FY2022 807.0, FY2025 1,032.8. Owner and reported FCF CAGRs are effectively identical because SBC is ~0.3% of net sales. All revenue growth since FY2021 is price/mix: volume fell from 84.0m hl to 72.8m hl (-13%) while net sales per hl rose from 122 to 153 (+25%).

scenario_narratives.base: The US beer category keeps shrinking and Molson Coors keeps giving up a little share to Constellation's imports, so financial volume falls 2-3% a year; net sales per hectolitre, which has risen ~6% a year since FY2021, slows to 2-3% and just offsets it. Net sales dip 1% in FY2027, flatten, and settle at +0.5%. The EBITDA margin on net sales, which fell from 22.2% (FY2024) to ~18.9% (FY2026E) on volume deleverage and ~US$130m of aluminium Midwest Premium cost, recovers only to 19.5%: Horizon 2030 savings and some tariff relief are largely reinvested in marketing or lost to deleverage. Capex holds at 6% of net sales (brewing network plus the ERP programme). Cash tax climbs from 13% to 22% of EBIT as accelerated deductions unwind. Terminal value is capped at 12x year-10 FCF, which binds below Gordon (14.4x at 7.5%/0.5%).
scenario_narratives.bull: The downturn proves more cyclical than structural: household budgets and Hispanic consumer spending recover, volume declines ease to about 1%, and the premiumisation runway in the US (Madri, Blue Moon, Peroni) together with Beyond Beer (Monaco RTD cocktails, Topo Chico, Fever-Tree, ZOA; ~10% of net sales) lifts net sales to +1.5% a year. Aluminium tariffs ease and the Americas restructuring and ERP savings drop through, taking the EBITDA margin back to 21.5%, roughly FY2025 and still below FY2024's 22.2%. This needs several independent things to go right at once (trade policy, category, execution under a new CEO), which is why it carries the lowest weight. Terminal value capped at 14x (Gordon 16.9x).
scenario_narratives.bear: GLP-1 adoption, moderation, cannabis substitution and generational change make the decline structural, and the core and value brands (Coors Light, Miller Lite, Keystone) lose share faster than the category. Volume falls ~5% a year; with promotion intensifying, price/mix covers only half of it and net sales fall 2-3% a year, ending 19% below FY2026. Fixed brewing costs and structurally higher aluminium costs take the EBITDA margin to 16%; capex cannot fall in step because the network is fixed. With US$5.4bn of net debt the equity takes the whole hit: leverage on this path rises from ~2.6x toward 3.5x+ EBITDA unless buybacks stop, against a 4.0x covenant. Terminal value capped at 10x (Gordon 11.6x at -1% growth). The terminal FCF stays positive; the zero floor is not hit.

valuation_philosophy.summary: Molson Coors is valued as a no-growth cash generator with financial leverage, not as a turnaround. The base case gives no credit for a return to FY2024 margins and caps the exit at 12x unlevered owner FCF. Because net debt is ~40% of enterprise value, the equity value is highly geared to the margin and volume path: the spread between bear and bull is wide, and the weighting leans to the bear side. Revenue throughout is net sales after excise taxes.
key_risks_to_valuation: Structural rather than cyclical US beer volume decline (GLP-1, moderation, demographics); every 1pt of EBITDA margin is worth roughly US$5/share
Aluminium Midwest Premium tariff cost (~US$130m in FY2026) persisting or rising; the base case assumes only partial relief
Leverage: net debt US$5.4bn (~2.6x FY2026E EBITDA) amplifies any shortfall in the bear path; covenant ceiling 4.0x
Cash tax normalisation: taxes paid are 8-13% of EBIT today; if the ramp to 22% arrives sooner the early-year flows are overstated
Further impairments of the US$11.8bn of intangibles do not affect cash but signal management's own lower outlook, as the Q3-2025 goodwill charge did
Execution risk from the CEO transition, the ERP implementation and the CDC distribution litigation

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API at inputs.price_as_of (regular session close); 52-week range 35.52-54.82
data_sources.financials: TAP_Metrics.csv / core_metrics and kpis (NetSales, buybacks, cash_taxes, ebitda_da); FY2025 10-K and Q3-2026 10-Q (balance sheet 30 Sep 2026, share counts 29 Oct 2026) in research/TAP/Extracted
data_sources.qualitative: TAP_Analysis.json (2026-11-15): Q3-2026 guidance cut, Horizon 2030, aluminium tariffs, category trends

inputs.share_count_basis: Q3-2026 10-Q cover, 29 Oct 2026: Class A 2.563m + Class B 173.018m + Class A exchangeable 2.679m + Class B exchangeable 7.094m = 185.35m, plus 0.3m dilutive share-based awards (Q3-2026 EPS note) = 185.7m. Held FLAT: SBC is expensed in the flows. The count has in fact been falling (209.9m FY2024 -> 186.8m Q3-2026 weighted diluted) because buybacks run far above SBC; no credit is taken for that.
inputs.sbc_source: Cash-flow statement share-based compensation add-back, TTM to 30 Sep 2026 (FY2025 35.0 - 9M-2025 27.2 + 9M-2026 26.2). Cash taxes withheld on net-share settlement are not separately disclosed in the filings parsed; at 0.3% of net sales the omission is immaterial.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD flows, USD rate. 10-year US Treasury ~4.3% + 5.0% ERP x levered beta ~0.95 = cost of equity ~9.0%; pre-tax cost of debt ~5.0% (2026 refinancing at current market rates), ~3.9% after tax; market-value weights ~56% equity / 44% debt give ~6.8%. Rounded UP to 7.5% so the valuation does not lean on today's leverage as a permanent subsidy. The same 7.5% is used in all three scenarios: business risk is carried by the scenario paths and weights, not by a per-scenario discount rate.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP. Operating lease cost stays inside EBITDA (operating lease liabilities are small, ~US$50m current portion scale); finance lease liabilities (~US$65m) are inside total_debt. No separate lease line in the flows.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100% of RMMC/RMBC and other partly owned entities). Noncontrolling interests (182.1) and redeemable noncontrolling interests (94.4) are deducted at 30 Sep 2026 book value in the equity bridge. Charged once.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, three scenarios, via the Drivers route. Routing: standard operating company (brewer); no memory entry, first valuation. REVENUE BASIS IS NET SALES, not the CSV `Revenue` column: that column is XBRL gross sales before excise taxes (FY2025 13,040.3) while net sales is 11,140.8 (kpis.NetSales, confirmed against the FY2025 10-K income statement line 4360). Every margin and percent path here is on net sales. FY0 is FY2026E, not the last full year: nine months of FY2026 are actual and the 30 Sep 2026 balance sheet already contains the cash they produced, so year 1 of the build is FY2027. base_revenue 10,990 = 9M-2026 actual 8,374.1 + Q4 estimate 2,616 (Q4-2025 2,662.4 less ~1.75%), consistent with guidance of -1% to -2% constant currency. The Q4-2026 cash flow (~US$150m on guidance) is counted neither in net debt nor in the flows, a small deliberate conservatism (~US$0.8/share). EBITDA anchor: operating income before goodwill impairment and other operating items, plus D&A: FY2024 2,578 (22.2%), FY2025 2,355 (21.1%), 9M-2026 1,600 (19.1%) vs 9M-2025 1,815 (21.4%); FY2026E ~2,075 (18.9%). reported_fcf is TTM to 30 Sep 2026 (OCF 1,821.1 - capex 651.9); FY2026 guidance is underlying FCF ~US$1.0bn +/-10%, which is levered (after ~US$240m interest paid) while the model's flows are unlevered. Interest income not stripped: the company is in net debt. Buybacks (TTM 570.0, actual cash in financing) fund far more than a flat count. Cash tax: taxes paid were 227 (FY2024), 131 (FY2025, OBBBA accelerated recovery) and 62 for 9M-2026, i.e. 8-13% of EBIT against a ~23% book rate; the path ramps to 22% of EBIT by year 7 because accelerated deductions are timing, not permanent (deferred tax liability 2,398). Working capital: payables (2,993) exceed receivables plus inventory (1,806), so a shrinking top line consumes cash and growth releases it; wc_capture is +10% of the change in net sales. Not in the bridge: overfunded pension plans (trapped surplus), the ~US$88m Fever-Tree stake and equity-method investments (equity income is already inside operating income).

bear.narrative: The category decline is structural and Molson Coors keeps losing share: volume -5% a year, pricing power fades as promotion intensifies, and fixed-cost deleverage takes the margin to 16%.

base.narrative: Volume keeps falling 2-3% a year and price/mix of 2-3% only just offsets it. Margin stays near the FY2026 trough and recovers about 0.7pt, well short of FY2024-25.

bull.narrative: Volume decline slows to ~1%, premium mix and Beyond Beer carry net sales to +1.5%, and the aluminium tariff cost plus restructuring savings restore the FY2025 margin.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear raised from the 15% default to 30%: five straight years of category volume decline, share loss faster than the category, and all four FY2026 guidance metrics cut again at Q3 make the structural reading a live possibility rather than a tail. Base 50%: flat net sales on falling volume is what the last three years actually delivered. Bull cut from 35% to 20%: it needs tariff relief, a category recovery and clean execution of Horizon 2030 by a new CEO at the same time.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
